title: Annotation curation daybook — edge cleanup notes
content: Personal daybook for ad-hoc heuristics, quick adjudication notes, and small triage decisions. Mostly shorthand. Goal: capture instincts + examples so future rounds can flip into a short rules doc later. Top-level goals (reminder): - Keep label set conservative: prefer fewer but higher-precision spans for first-pass. - Flag ambiguous examples with helpful example-based guidance rather than blanket rules. - When in doubt, capture canonical / normalized form as additional metadata field (if pipeline allows) rather than changing span boundaries. Quick heuristics (operational): 1) Overlapping company/person spans - If one span is clearly an honorific + last name ("Dr. Patel") and the other is full name ("Dr. Sameer Patel"), prefer full-name span. - If short span is an acronym contained in long span ("OpenAI" inside "OpenAI Research Lab"), label the longer span but add alias=\"OpenAI\" as metadata where possible. 2) Currency + unit noise - Preserve original token sequence for token-level audits, but normalize separate fields: amount_numeric, currency_code. - Samples: Raw: "€1.200,50" -> amount_numeric: "1200.50", currency_code: "EUR" Raw: "$1,234.00 (USD)" -> amount_numeric: "1234.00", currency_code: "USD" - Heuristic: detect locale separators (".," vs ",.") heuristically by presence of currency symbol and digit groups; fall back to human review for ambiguous formats. 3) Noisy transcripts / filler words - Remove filler tokens from entity spans ("uh", "um", repeated dashes) unless they change meaning. - Example: "um John Smith" -> span: "John Smith". Keep a "raw_span" field for provenance. 4) Partial-label policy (when annotator marks partial overlaps) - If a candidate span overlaps >= 70% token coverage of a canonical entity, accept and mark as "partial_confirmed". - <70% -> send to adjudication queue with 3 sample neighbors for context. Example adjudication entries (copy into triage queue): - ID: daybook-001 Raw: "Sent from support-team@acme.co on 2023-05-09" Candidate labels: EMAIL: "support-team@acme.co" OR ORG: "acme.co" Decision: prefer EMAIL for single token with @; add ORG alias by domain extraction. - ID: daybook-002 Raw: "When we say 'the bank', which org? Wells or First National?" Candidate labels: ORG ambiguous -> require doc-level resolution, mark as 'ambiguous-org' until doc metadata supplied. Span examples (bad -> better): - Bad: label COMPANY: "Acme" when context requires "Acme, Inc." Better: COMPANY: "Acme, Inc." with alias: ["Acme"] - Bad: label ADDRESS: "5th Ave" when full address is present across tokens with PO box nearby Better: capture full address span, mark subspan "5th Ave" as LOCATION_SUBPART. HTML / markup noise - Strip obvious HTML tags from spans but capture them in raw_text. Eg: "Acme" -> span: "Acme". If tags convey semantics (like or ) keep a note in metadata: markup_tag=["a"] Multilingual partials - If entity split across language boundaries (EN/ES): keep single contiguous span if tokens are adjacent and represent same logical entity. Add lang_hint if script differs. Adjudicator quick checklist (for messy items): - Is the span semantically self-contained? - Does normalization fix the issue (currency/date canonicalization)? If yes, prefer normalization + keep span. - Would adding an alias / metadata preserve downstream behavior better than changing span? Prefer metadata when safe. Open questions / TODOs (prioritized): - Q1: How do we treat abbreviated legal suffixes in another language ("S.A.", "GmbH") when annotators vary on inclusion? Proposed: default include if token adjacent to name, but add rule to collapse common suffix variants in normalization step. - Q2: Should we add a "confidence_hint" token-level tag when an annotator marks uncertain? (Useful for active learning sampling). - Q3: Edgecase: timestamps lacking year. Many logs have dates like "Mar 3 10:21"; for annotation, we currently leave as literal. Consider heuristics to infer year from doc metadata. Micro examples for sanity-check training set (copy-paste friendly): 1) "Refund issued: GBP 45.00 to kevin.o'reilly@example.com" Labels: AMOUNT: "GBP 45.00" -> amount_numeric: "45.00", currency_code: "GBP"; EMAIL: "kevin.o'reilly@example.com" 2) "Call with Dr. S. Kwon—rescheduled" Labels: PERSON: "Dr. S. Kwon"; prefer including honorific when present. 3) "Order #4567 (Acme Corp.) shipped" Labels: ORDER_ID: "#4567"; ORG: "Acme Corp." (include parenthesis cleanup) Short-term tags to add to pipeline: ["partial_confirmed","ambiguous-org","markup_stripped","locale_amount"] (these are adhoc — will be formalized later). Notes to self: keep this daybook minimal; move stable heuristics to a living doc in shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/labeling-guides once we have consensus. When moving, include representative examples and failure cases (with ticket refs). Random thought: build a tiny CLI that given raw token sequence suggests canonicalization + a "why" explanation (rule id + sample match). Would speed up adjudication. End of entry for 2025-02-11.
